races.name: CopyBet Proudly Backs UK Horse Racing Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Eternal Angel
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who steps up to lead from a prominent base; Tom Lacey's 6yo has won twice on Good ground at 16f and her hurdling experience gives her a clear edge in controlling the race, though she is technically racing slightly out of role at lead versus her natural prominent position — a minor caveat.|

runners_data.name: Aimeric
runners_data.note: Jennie Candlish's 7yo has a sound record in going-similar conditions (4/16f Good finish, 4th on debut here) but is a true hold-up horse whose instinct will be to settle last; Lewis Stones (3) must manage the redistribution reality that she will likely race closer to midfield than ideal, which may neutralise her finishing kick.|

runners_data.name: Arcon
runners_data.note: Won on Good at 14f and has hurdles experience (hg:p), making him one of the more likely beneficiaries if pace collapse opens the race up; another Candlish hold-up type who will be shuffled further forward than he prefers — Luke Scott (3) must adapt quickly on a horse whose last two hurdles runs have been deep in the field.|

runners_data.name: Happy Harrison
runners_data.note: Gary Hanmer's 6yo has three runs on Good and has shown 0W0P from them, making him a consistent underperformer on this surface; wears a tongue tie and is a genuine hold-up type, but the complete absence of wins or places makes it hard to build a case even if the pace scenario suits.|

runners_data.name: Ride Like A Girl
runners_data.note: Gavin Sheehan partners this consistent Jamie Snowden 5yo who has won twice on Good at exactly 16f — the perfect profile for this race shape; her natural prominent style means she should sit a length or two off Eternal Angel without drama, and her course-equivalent form is the standout statistical argument in the field.|

runners_data.name: Dancingondiamonds
runners_data.note: Sean Bowen is a high-calibre booking for Olly Murphy's lightly raced 4yo, whose only hurdle run was an 8th on Good at 16f — thin evidence but not alarming; by nature a hold-up/front-foot type (hg:ht), he is one of the horses most likely to find himself racing against instinct if the pace compresses the field into a tight bunch.|

runners_data.name: Mystic Wind
runners_data.note: Dan Skelton's 4yo is trained by one of the sharpest yards in novice hurdling (T14: 17/31) and Harry Skelton ensures maximum assistance in the saddle; with only two runs and 0W0P on Good, the case rests almost entirely on trainer/jockey quality and the hope she's better than shown — a genuine hold-up type who will need the race to be run to suit her.|

runners_data.name: Rose Warrior
runners_data.note: Ian Power rides this Candlish 4yo who returns from a 43-day break following a fall last time (LR: 43F); her hurdles form includes a 7th on Good at 12f and her chasing profile (hg:p) suggests jumping confidence may be variable post-fall — a significant watch factor before assessing tactical suitability.|

runners_data.name: Amalfina
runners_data.note: Jonathan Burke takes the ride for D J Jeffreys, whose stable is quiet (T14: 0/3); this 4yo's entire form profile is on Soft or Heavy, making today's Good ground a genuine unknown, and her one hurdles run was a 7th on Good at 16f — a true hold-up type who will be carried wider in the pack than she ideally wants.|

runners_data.name: Pearl Knot
runners_data.note: Toby Wynne partners this Oliver Greenall & Josh Guerriero 4yo who is lightly raced and unseated (U) on her only form figure, returning just 11 days later — minimal intelligence to work with, and the quick turnaround after an exit means jumping reliability must be flagged as the primary concern in this field.|

races.paceDynamic: Eternal Angel is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner novices' hurdle and, with no genuine rival willing to press from the front, she should be able to dictate a sustainable, unhurried gallop around Uttoxeter's 2m trip on Good ground. Ride Like A Girl is the most naturally prominent of the chasing pack and is likely to track Eternal Angel closely from the off, creating a two-horse front group rather than a true solo breakaway. The bulk of the field — Aimeric, Arcon, Dancingondiamonds, Amalfina — are genuine hold-up types who have been redistributed into midfield on the map because this race simply cannot accommodate all of them at the rear; of those, Arcon and Aimeric (both Candlish-trained) are best equipped to get closest to their natural position, with Dancingondiamonds and Amalfina likely to find themselves further forward than ideal. A controlled, single-pace gallop on Good ground over 2m at Uttoxeter historically rewards horses who travel prominently and quicken from the front two or three, meaning horses able to sit just off Eternal Angel and produce a decisive jump at the second-last will be most favoured — prominent trackers and those with a turn of foot from a handy position hold the clearest tactical edge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Eternal Angel Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Eternal Angel bowls along at a comfortable clip and Ride Like A Girl tracks without applying pressure, the pace is honest but never punishing.
scenarios.body: Eternal Angel sets the fractions, keeps the field honest without burning herself out, and the race is run at a tempo that suits those travelling smoothly in the first three; Ride Like A Girl and any other prominent runner who can land a blow jumping the last two flights are the primary beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If Eternal Angel's pace is just slow enough to set up a sprint finish from the second-last, a well-positioned tracker with a sharp turn of foot pounces.
scenarios.body: Ride Like A Girl, with her consistent form on identical Good ground at 2m (5 of last 5 runs on Good, two wins), is ideally placed to exploit any let-up and hit the flat with momentum; Aimeric, if managing to sit closer than her redistribution suggests, carries enough class at OR 120 to land a late blow.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Delivers Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the straight and the front-runners tie up, a genuine deep closer coming from off the pace delivers a late run.
scenarios.body: Arcon and Mystic Wind are the most credible beneficiaries if the race falls apart late, though both are operating well outside their natural hold-up comfort zone given the redistribution in this field; Harry Skelton aboard Mystic Wind (T14: 17/31) and the Candlish pair give this scenario some trainer/jockey plausibility, but it remains a low-probability shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — Pace Collapse or Falls
scenarios.trigger: If Pearl Knot (unseated last time) or another runner causes disruption, or Eternal Angel over-jumps and the race loses its shape entirely.
scenarios.body: Without a reliable pacesetter the race becomes a tactical crawl that rewards the most adaptable jumper in the field; Happy Harrison and Rose Warrior, both lightly tried, are complete unknowns who could profit from a scrambled finish but their form figures offer little confidence.

watchPoints.text: Pearl Knot unseated on her only start and returns within 11 days — watch her at the first hurdle as any jumping error could bring down other runners in a 10-horse field.
Rose Warrior fell last time out (LR: 43F) and race experience over hurdles on Good ground is thin — monitor her jumping confidence early, particularly at the cross-hurdles mid-race.

Eternal Angel's controlled front-running dictates the shape of the entire race; if she is outpaced off the bend or makes a jumping error, the race loses its structure and late chaos becomes far more likely.

The Candlish triple (Aimeric, Arcon, Rose Warrior) means the same yard has three runners whose tactics may affect each other — watch whether any of the three is allowed to drift closer than expected, which could compromise the others' running lines.|

Ride Like A Girl's prominent style and 2W from 5 runs on Good at exactly 16f make her the most form-consistent horse in the field for this specific scenario — watch how quickly Gavin Sheehan positions her behind Eternal Angel in the opening half-mile.|

races.name: CopyBet Daily World Cup Profit Boost Novices' Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Gaelic Rambler
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up performer whose recent form (U3225-) shows consistency without a win; Jonjo O'Neill Jr takes the ride but the 77-day absence and a tendency to finish third or fifth rather than close suggests he needs everything to fall right late.|

runners_data.name: That's Nice
runners_data.note: Nicky Henderson handler (0 wins from 3 last 14 days) and Harry Cobden partnership is reliable, but three placings from nine good-ground runs with no win on that surface is a concern; sits naturally at the back and needs the race to fall apart in front of him.|

runners_data.name: Hudson
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with OR=108 but marked STYLE_FIT 0.93, indicating he tends to race more prominently than ideally — James Bowen will use him to control the tempo and he could pinch a big advantage if rivals are slow to react; outright winner if the race is run to suit him.|

runners_data.name: Jiair Madrik
runners_data.note: Sharply in form with two recent wins over similar good-ground distances (1/20f/GOO, 1/21f/GOO), Theo Gillard is a capable claimer for Donald McCain; head-tack headgear and a prominent style make him the most natural beneficiary of a sole front-runner race shape.|

runners_data.name: Seeitoldya
runners_data.note: Runs genuinely from hold-up, but the map places him ahead of his true position because the field is saturated with back-runners; a 103-day absence, a modest recent string (545U0-), and a trainer who has gone 0 from 11 in the last fortnight all weigh against him here.|

runners_data.name: Back In The Bay
runners_data.note: Two wins from nine good-ground starts and proven at 2m on this surface, Jonathan Burke can place him handily; at heart a hold-up runner pushed into apparent midfield on the positional map only by the volume of closers, though his all-round versatility means he handles a range of positions.|

runners_data.name: The Clonmel Kid
runners_data.note: Philip Kirby's horse has a sound good-ground profile (1W4P from 13 runs) and is capable of sitting mid-to-rear by nature, but a headgear note (p) and the fact he was beaten into sixth last time suggest he is not hitting top form; Joe Williamson is an inexperienced pilot for a competitive handicap.|

runners_data.name: Ice Jet
runners_data.note: Three consecutive wins at 2m on good ground give Dan Skelton's four-year-old strong claims as the classiest closer in the race; Harry Skelton is one of the sharpest jockeys at placing a horse from the back, though the step up to 2m4f from all-2m form introduces a genuine query.|

races.paceDynamic: Hudson is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival to push him, is expected to bowl along at a manageable gallop on good ground over 2m4f at Uttoxeter — a track that rewards horses who travel well through a race rather than those who need a sprint finish. Jiair Madrik is the likeliest horse to sit close to Hudson in second or third, with the remainder of the field — Gaelic Rambler, That's Nice, Ice Jet, Seeitoldya, Back In The Bay, and The Clonmel Kid — all natural hold-up or midfield types who will be settled behind. The redistributed horses (Ice Jet, Seeitoldya, Back In The Bay, The Clonmel Kid) are genuine hold-up or at-best-midfield animals pushed forward on the positional map simply because so many closers contest this race — Hudson is almost certain to control the early tempo unchallenged. A single, unhurried pace-setter dictating a sustainable gallop on good ground heavily favours horses who travel prominently and have enough class to quicken from mid-race onward, particularly Jiair Madrik who can track Hudson throughout; pure hold-up finishers face a tougher task if the pace never becomes genuinely searching.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hudson Controls, Jiair Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Hudson sets a steady, uncontested lead and Jiair Madrik tracks him throughout before asserting from two out.
scenarios.body: Hudson bowls along at his own rhythm, setting a tempo that suits a horse travelling prominently, and Jiair Madrik — a two-time recent winner over similar good-ground trips — pounces having sat just off the pace the whole way.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Ice Jet Strikes From Midfield
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely honest enough to stretch the field and Ice Jet, full of confidence from three straight wins, picks them off late.
scenarios.body: Harry Skelton will have Ice Jet settled just off the main group, and three wins at 2m on good ground suggest the four-year-old has the class to reel in any front-runners if they empty late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Back In The Bay Capitalises
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes truly steady and the field bunches, allowing Back In The Bay to produce a well-timed run from a good position.
scenarios.body: Back In The Bay has won at this distance on good ground and is a versatile front-to-midfield performer who can sit handily off a slow pace; Jonathan Burke is experienced enough to place him perfectly if gaps appear.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Ambush Late
scenarios.trigger: If Hudson sets an unexpectedly strong gallop and opens the race up for the true hold-up runners sweeping through beaten horses.
scenarios.body: Gaelic Rambler or That's Nice — both natural hold-up types under quality riders in Jonjo O'Neill Jr and Harry Cobden — could finish strongly if attrition thins the field, though neither's form at this trip on good ground is particularly convincing.

watchPoints.text: Watch Hudson in the early stages — if James Bowen is allowed to bowl along completely unchallenged, he could build a lead large enough to make him very difficult to catch even for horses with superior finishing ability.

Ice Jet is unbeaten in three at 2m on good ground but has never raced beyond 2m; watch how Harry Skelton deploys him once they turn for home — if the extra four furlongs finds him out, the pattern of the race could change dramatically late.

Jiair Madrik is fitted with head-tack and has won twice recently — if he travels as well as his form suggests, watch for Theo Gillard making his move sooner than rivals expect, potentially turning this into a two-horse race between himself and Hudson from the third-last.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up horses (Seeitoldya, Back In The Bay, The Clonmel Kid, Ice Jet) will all be fighting for similar ground on the final bend — watch for traffic issues or interference if the race compresses heading to the straight.

Gaelic Rambler's 77-day absence after a run of placed efforts is worth noting — if Jonjo O'Neill Jr gives him a confidence-building ride rather than an aggressive one, he will be suited by any late attrition but is unlikely to be a factor if the race is run cleanly.

races.name: Peter Smith Birthday Celebration Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Karnaval Point
runners_data.note: Won twice already this season on Good ground and sits top of the weights at OR 119 — the confirmed front-runner who should control every yard of this 3m trip; David Pipe's yard is in solid form (5/9 T14) and Corcoran's booking looks deliberate, though STYLE_FIT of 0.91 flags it is nominally classified as prominent rather than a true tearaway, a minor nuance that barely changes the picture here.

runners_data.name: Ivane
runners_data.note: Jonathan Burke takes the ride on this OR 117 eight-year-old who has solid sim-going form (9/15, 3W 7P) and a race record showing consistent placement at 3m+ trips; naturally wants to race prominently and is realistic about securing a forward position here given the compressed field, though all recent form has come on Soft ground which is worth monitoring even on today's Good surface.

runners_data.name: Paper Mill
runners_data.note: Stuart Edmunds' 10-year-old returns from a 164-day absence — the longest layoff in the field — having won over 26f on Soft last time out; it is a genuine prominent racer by nature, but with five rivals all seeking forward positions the likelihood of getting its preferred slot is reduced, and the fitness question after nearly six months off is the primary concern regardless of positional dynamics.

runners_data.name: Fairlawn Flyer
runners_data.note: Mickey Bowen's gelding ran just 11 days ago and arrives race-fit, showing consistent placing on Good ground (7/15 sim-going, 2W 4P) and posting three placings from five recent starts; it races with a hood and wants to be forward but the overflow of prominent types means it is likely to find itself further back than ideal, tempering its chance in this particular shape given its STYLE_FIT of 0.92.

runners_data.name: Eaton Anne
runners_data.note: Sean Bowen takes the mount for Olly Murphy (5/12 T14) on this OR 110 mare wearing tongue-tie and visor, whose recent form of 524-20 is modest and whose sim-going record (4/15, 0W 1P) is uninspiring; pushed back to a hold-up position by the pace map, this is against the grain of her natural forward-going style, and the combination of form regression and forced positional compromise makes her outlook difficult.

runners_data.name: A Dublin Job
runners_data.note: Sarah-Jayne Davies' nine-year-old has strong form on Good ground (11/15 sim-going, 3W 5P), winning twice over 20f on the surface and placing once over 22f, and James Best is a capable handler; it is a front-runner/prominent type by record but the field leaves it mapped to midfield — the question is whether it can muscle into a forward position early enough to use that Good-ground form productively over this 3m trip.

races.paceDynamic: Karnaval Point is the one confirmed front-runner in this six-runner field and should dictate from the outset over 3m on Good ground at Uttoxeter, setting a sustainable gallop without any genuine rival pressing for the lead. With five of the six runners naturally wanting to race prominently, the reality is that only Karnaval Point can secure the front, leaving Paper Mill, Fairlawn Flyer, A Dublin Job, Ivane, and Eaton Anne all jostling for a compressed berth behind — several will race further back than they ideally want. This field holds more front-running and prominent types than the shape can accommodate; of those, Ivane and A Dublin Job are most likely to actually secure a position close to the pace given their typical racing patterns and race fitness, while Paper Mill (164 days off), Fairlawn Flyer, and Eaton Anne risk being shuffled back against their nature. A controlled, one-pace gallop set by Karnaval Point strongly favours a horse that can travel prominently behind the leader and produce a clean round of jumping — the prominent-to-lead profile is the one to side with, with hold-up types at a structural disadvantage given none of the genuine closers in this field are authentic hold-up horses.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Karnaval Point Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Karnaval Point jumps cleanly and dictates an uncontested, honest gallop from the front.
scenarios.body: Karnaval Point, trained by David Pipe and ridden by Rian Corcoran, sets every fraction on Good ground over a trip it has won at already, with no rival able or willing to mount a serious challenge for the lead; a clean round of jumping from a horse rated OR 119 in a 6-runner field is a potent combination.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Challenger Overhauling Late
scenarios.trigger: If Karnaval Point begins to tire approaching the last and a prominent tracker uses a better jumping round to wear it down.
scenarios.body: With the pace honest but not frantic, a horse like Ivane or A Dublin Job — travelling close to the leader throughout — is best placed to capitalise if Karnaval Point flattens out on the run-in; both have placed form at this trip and distance on comparable ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Steady Pace Suits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is unexpectedly slow, compressing the field and turning this into a sprint-finish off a false pace.
scenarios.body: A truly dawdling tempo could allow Fairlawn Flyer or Eaton Anne — both pushed back from their natural positions — to arrive with a seemingly fresh challenge at the last two fences; however, this scenario depends on horses racing out of their natural role and is structurally less reliable because none are true hold-up types.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Attrition Chase Errors Decide
scenarios.trigger: If fencing errors or departures in the middle stages reshuffle the field and reward a horse that simply completes efficiently.
scenarios.body: Over 3m at Uttoxeter in a small field, jumping errors are a genuine variable — Paper Mill has the form to capitalise on a carnage-shortened race if it rediscovers fitness after 164 days off, and A Dublin Job's course-and-distance form over Good ground stands up if rivals fall away.

watchPoints.text: Karnaval Point's jumping under pressure — if it makes a significant error at a fence in the back straight, the lead could evaporate and the entire probable shape collapses.

Paper Mill's fitness after 164 days off is the biggest unknown in the field; watch the ring for market moves that suggest connections are confident, otherwise treat it as a qualifier rather than a live contender.

The scramble for prominent positions early could create a falsely-rushed first circuit — if Ivane, A Dublin Job, and Fairlawn Flyer all push to get close to Karnaval Point, the pace dynamic could become more contested than anticipated, working against front-runner favourites.

Eaton Anne's positional reality — Sean Bowen aboard a horse mapped to hold-up but naturally prominent; how far back she ends up settling in the early stages will tell you quickly whether her race is already compromised.

A Dublin Job's ability to assert early and claim a genuine prominent slot is worth watching at the first fence; if Best gets it travelling close to the pace, its Good-ground form profile over this trip makes it one of the more interesting positional plays in the race.

races.name: CopyBet Support Safer Gambling Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Roger Pol
runners_data.note: Jamie Snowden runner who has won twice over 24f on Good ground and has course form, but he steps up markedly in trip here and is technically a prominent horse fulfilling the front-runner role — his STYLE_FIT tag reflects that and he may find the longer stamina test exposing late.|

runners_data.name: Sunray Shadow
runners_data.note: Hat-trick scorer in excellent current form, Dan Skelton's string in fine fettle (T14: 12/23), and Harry Skelton's tactical nous means he will secure his prominent position without fuss — six wins from 12 runs on Good ground underlines this surface suits him well.|

runners_data.name: Lipa K
runners_data.note: Jack Tudor partner who has won twice on Good ground at 25f and was placed at this sort of trip last season — ran poorly on seasonal return (9th) but was fine before that, and his 43-day break combined with a tongue-tie suggests connections have had a prep target in mind.|

runners_data.name: Ernest Gray
runners_data.note: Alan King runner fresh off a 94-day break and carrying blinkers, who finished 1st and 2nd on Good ground at 23-24f earlier in his profile — but his last two runs produced back-to-back 6ths and his Good-ground record recently reads only 2W3P from 6 qualifying runs.|

runners_data.name: Smugglers Haven
runners_data.note: Strong form figures on Good ground (4W8P from 11 runs) and won last time out; genuinely wants to race up with the pace but, with so many prominent types in this field, Miss Lily Bradstock's 7lb claim may not be enough positional authority to hold a prominent berth naturally.|

runners_data.name: Champagne Twist
runners_data.note: Ben Pauling runner who managed a placed effort last time after a sequence of failures and falls — his Good-ground form is thin (1W2P from 5 runs) and he wants to be involved early, but in a field of this composition he is likely to be shuffled back from his preferred spot.|

runners_data.name: Stumps Or Slips
runners_data.note: Sean Bowen booking is a strong plus — this horse has a flawless Good-ground record (15/15 qualifying runs on that surface, 6W9P) and has won back-to-back, going over 24f previously; the step back up in trip suits and he is a genuine player whose profile fits Scenario A and B alike.|

runners_data.name: Maghlaak
runners_data.note: Mark Walford horse returning from 193 days off (fell last time), last won on Soft ground over 20f and has only two placed runs from nine Good-ground starts — the combination of a long absence, style mismatch and weak Good-ground form makes him a risky proposition here.|

runners_data.name: Abbey Scope
runners_data.note: Nicky Richards six-year-old who has won two of his last three starts on Good ground and looks progressive at this level — but he is a natural front-runner who will find himself tucked back in what is a congested prominent group, meaning he races out of role unless he can assert early.|

runners_data.name: Jet Of Magic
runners_data.note: 202-day absence for Steph Cameron's ten-year-old is the most immediate concern — his last winning run came over 22f on Good ground three runs ago, and a hold-up style in a race unlikely to fall apart late does not set him up ideally off such a lay-off.|

runners_data.name: Hillview
runners_data.note: Gary Hanmer's veteran holds very modest recent form (four finishes of 4th or worse, two PUs in last five) and Benjamin Macey's 5lb claim does not materially change his prospects — hold-up style, long trip and consistent under-performance in this grade make him hard to support.|

runners_data.name: Dr Seb
runners_data.note: Olly Murphy's nine-year-old won twice on Good ground at 24f in his prime but his last two runs produced 6th and 8th — a 94-day break and a redistribution to midfield from his natural prominent position means he races away from his best tactical conditions here.|

races.paceDynamic: Roger Pol is the lone confirmed front-runner here and, with no obvious challenger for the lead, he should dictate a sustainable gallop from the front over this 2m7½f trip on Good ground at Uttoxeter. Sunray Shadow, Lipa K, Ernest Gray and Stumps Or Slips are all genuine prominent types who will press forward behind him, creating a compact, organised head of the field rather than a truly contested pace. The field actually contains more prominent-types than the race shape can accommodate: Smugglers Haven, Champagne Twist, Abbey Scope and Dr Seb are all natural front-runners or pressers who are most likely to end up racing out of role in mid-division, with Stumps Or Slips and Sunray Shadow best-placed to physically secure the prominent positions behind Roger Pol. A sustainable, even tempo on Good ground over a stamina trip strongly favours horses who can race handy and travel fluently — prominent types with proven course-and-distance form and the class to quicken from the front rank will be at a structural advantage, while genuine hold-up horses face the risk of having too much ground to make up in a race unlikely to fall apart late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Front, Prominent Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Roger Pol sets a fair pace unchallenged and Sunray Shadow, Stumps Or Slips and Lipa K travel handy throughout.
scenarios.body: Roger Pol's uncontested lead produces a rhythm that suits horses racing in the first four, with the Good ground ensuring no dramatic late collapse to bring closers into play; Sunray Shadow's hat-trick of wins and Harry Skelton's positional authority make this profile his ideal race shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Drifts, Stamina Test
scenarios.trigger: If Roger Pol sets a generous tempo from flag-fall that stretches the field over the long 2m7½f and takes its toll on prominent trackers.
scenarios.body: Those who conserve energy mid-race and possess the deepest stamina reserves gain a decisive edge as the race becomes a test of attrition in the final half-mile; Stumps Or Slips, who has won twice over 24f on Good ground and thrives in staying contests, benefits most here.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Reshuffled Prominents Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If one of the redistributed prominent types — Smugglers Haven, Champagne Twist or Abbey Scope — manages to push forward and secure their natural position despite the crowded front rank.
scenarios.body: Winning the tactical battle for position early would allow the redistribution horse to race within themselves and deploy their natural jumping fluency; Smugglers Haven's strong Good-ground record (4W8P) and recent win give this the best chance of any redistributed runner materialising.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Finish Through
scenarios.trigger: If an unusually strong, honest gallop is set and the race genuinely falls apart late enough for closers to pick up the pieces.
scenarios.body: Maghlaak or Jet Of Magic would need the field to string out dramatically and a significant gap to open between the last hurdle and the line; given the modest pace set by a lone front-runner without a challenger, this scenario is structurally unlikely and both horses carry long lay-offs as an added concern.

watchPoints.text: Sunray Shadow and Stumps Or Slips are both likely to push forward behind Roger Pol — if they travel fluently in the first four throughout, the race shape becomes extremely difficult to overcome from behind and either could command the finish.

Smugglers Haven, Abbey Scope and Champagne Twist are all natural prominent types who will contend for limited real estate behind Roger Pol in the early stages — watch for scrimmaging and positional losses at the first couple of flights that could compromise their races entirely.

Roger Pol's trip stamina is unproven at 2m7½f and, if he finds the final half-mile beyond him, he could stop quickly and cause interference — any prominent horse caught flat-footed behind a stopping leader at a hurdle late in the race is a legitimate danger watch.

Stumps Or Slips has run exclusively on Good ground in all 15 qualifying runs with an exceptional W/P record — any market drift here would be informative, as his profile is almost uniquely suited to today's conditions and trip.

Maghlaak and Jet Of Magic both return from absences of 193 and 202 days respectively — monitor how they move in the market; any significant support for either would suggest connections have done enough work at home to be confident, otherwise treat both as fitness queries.

races.name: CopyBet Pay First Past The Post Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Rocks Up Late
runners_data.note: Won last time out on Good ground over this exact C&D trip, handles the conditions well, and as the sole genuine front-runner will dictate tempo; the STYLE_FIT tag notes he is listed as Prominent rather than full Lead, but his race-shape control here is uncontested — treat with slight positional caution rather than a full discount.

runners_data.name: Jammy Jay
runners_data.note: 173 days off the track is a significant concern for Deutsch and Evans, whose yard has shown no winners from three runners in the past 14 days; a true hold-up type who needs pace to run into, and the controlled forecast tempo is not ideal for his profile.

runners_data.name: Iolaos Du Mou
runners_data.note: Worsley rides a horse with solid Good-ground form (12/14 runs on similar going, two wins) and hg:h headgear worn; genuine hold-up style but this scenario requires pace to develop that Rocks Up Late is unlikely to provide — 66 days off the track worth noting.

runners_data.name: Network Rgb
runners_data.note: Only three career runs, all on Soft ground, making his ability to handle Good turf a genuine unknown; Olly Murphy's charge is a 198-day absentee from a very small sample — Sean Bowen is a quality booking but the going and fitness question marks are real.

runners_data.name: Buxted Reel
runners_data.note: Lacey-trained prominent racer who finished second on Good ground at this trip 21 days ago — fresh enough and well-placed stylistically to track the leader; headgear-free and 160lbs suggests a competitive mark, though his win record in this style is limited (0W6P on similar going).

runners_data.name: Tara Iti
runners_data.note: hg:v (visor) worn and a natural hold-up type pushed into a midfield slot on the map due to overcrowding at the rear — Barry Brennan's horse has never won on Good ground in his last five tries on it, and the STYLE_FIT tag further tempers his chance in this shape.

runners_data.name: Colinski
runners_data.note: Rebecca Menzies sends a 4-year-old making just his third hurdle start, and though he ran third on Good ground last time, he is a natural hold-up horse who has been redistributed to midfield — the hg:p headgear (possibly first time) and a 3lb claim from Maggs are the angles to watch, not his likely race position.

runners_data.name: Huit Reflets
runners_data.note: Veteran of nine runs, Walford's 9-year-old was beaten into ninth last time on Good ground here (same trip) but placed twice over 20f on Soft — the step back in trip from those placed efforts and the going switch may not play to his strengths, though his prominent style suits the forecast shape.

runners_data.name: Cawthorne Banker
runners_data.note: Jonjo O'Neill Jr takes the ride on a horse who finished second on Good ground over this trip on his most recent win-track effort; hg:b (blinkers) worn, but as a redistributed hold-up type he is unlikely to get his favoured deep position — the jockey booking is the standout positive angle.

runners_data.name: Genbu
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with an excellent recent Good-ground profile (2W7P, three consecutive top-three finishes on Good); prominent style fits the forecast race shape well and Sarah-Jayne Davies' charge looks consistently competitive at this level — no headgear, fresh enough at 20 days.

runners_data.name: Whatcombe
runners_data.note: Faye Bramley's 4-year-old has never won (0W0P) and pulled up on most recent start; redistributed from a natural hold-up position to midfield on the map, and with the worst OR in the field at 81, this is a horse best watched rather than backed in this company.

races.paceDynamic: Rocks Up Late is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner 2m handicap hurdle on Good ground at Uttoxeter, and with no other genuine pace horse to challenge, he is expected to control proceedings from the front at a sustainable, measured tempo. Buxted Reel and Huit Reflets will press forward into prominent positions, giving the race a small cluster of horses near the pace but without anyone likely to force a genuinely searching early gallop. The field holds more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate — Colinski, Tara Iti, Cawthorne Banker and Whatcombe are all natural hold-up horses redistributed to midfield on the map, meaning genuine closers will be racing closer than ideal and their late kick may be partially neutralised. With one controlled pace-setter and Good ground that rewards those in the front rank, this race shape most strongly favours prominent racers who can track the leader, travel fluidly, and attack at the second-last — horses held up from a true rear position are structurally disadvantaged here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Front, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Rocks Up Late dictates a steady-to-moderate tempo unchallenged and the race only quickens from the third-last.
scenarios.body: Rocks Up Late stamps his authority from the front and those tucked in just behind — Buxted Reel, Genbu and Huit Reflets — are best placed to strike as the pace lifts entering the home straight; the controlled gallop means hold-up horses struggle to generate momentum from deep.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Holds, Front Runner Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo never quickens enough to peg back the leader and Rocks Up Late's recent winning form translates cleanly here.
scenarios.body: Rocks Up Late, who won last time on identical Good ground over this trip, simply bowls along in front and pings his hurdles, with the field unable to close the gap as the pace stays constant; his Pauling yard has two winners from 14 in the 14-day window and he carries the strongest recent form in the race.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Hosts Squeeze Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves sufficiently honest that a sharp-turning, well-placed midfield horse can thread through between the second-last and the last.
scenarios.body: Colinski or Cawthorne Banker — mapped mid-field despite being natural hold-up types — could benefit if they end up in a better position than their usual style dictates, with Jonjo O'Neill Jr's tactical awareness potentially allowing Cawthorne Banker to find a gap late; however both carry the [REDISTRIBUTED] discount and this scenario requires things to fall unusually well.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: True Closers Reel Field In
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is stronger than anticipated and the front rank tie each other up, leaving genuine hold-up horses with a clear closing run.
scenarios.body: Iolaos Du Mou and Jammy Jay are the only horses whose hold-up profiles are not flagged as redistributed, meaning they are the only true closers in the field; this scenario requires a faster-than-expected pace to materialise, which is unlikely given Rocks Up Late has no natural rival for the lead.

watchPoints.text: Rocks Up Late sets the race up entirely on his own terms — if he gets an uncontested lead and bowls along at his own pace, the rest of the field must chase him down over 2m Good ground, which is a major structural advantage.

Network Rgb has only run on Soft ground in his three career starts — Sean Bowen's booking suggests connections are confident, but a 198-day break combined with an unproven going profile on Good turf is a combination that warrants caution in a 11-runner field.

Jammy Jay's 173-day absence for a yard with zero winners from three recent runners is a red flag — Charlie Deutsch must produce this horse cold from a long break, and the hold-up style is poorly suited to the likely controlled tempo.

Colinski, Tara Iti, Cawthorne Banker and Whatcombe are all natural hold-up horses mapped to midfield positions they may not naturally secure — if they end up further back than the map suggests, any late run becomes even harder to deliver in what is likely to be a slowly-run 2m.

Genbu's three consecutive top-three finishes on Good ground, all over 16f, make him the most consistent recent Good-ground performer in the field — watch how quickly Charlie Price positions him behind the leader from the outset.

runners_data.name: Alshadhian
runners_data.note: OR 99, the joint-top-rated runner, has posted consistent form on Good ground (three of last four runs) including two seconds over this exact 16f trip; genuine hold-up horse who needs a strong pace to chase down, and the likely single pace-setter is a slight concern, but Harry Tudor has the tactical intelligence to place him well from the rear.

runners_data.name: Person Of Interest
runners_data.note: Harry Cobden takes the ride for an in-form trainer (Faye Bramley, T14 3/6) and this 6-year-old has run twelve of fifteen starts on similar going — solid surface fit — but finishing positions have been erratic (P, 4, 9, U, 6) and the hold-up style is genuinely vulnerable if Electric Eddy controls fractions from in front without being pressed.

runners_data.name: Electric Eddy
runners_data.note: The race's only confirmed front-runner, free to bowl along uncontested from the off; OR 94, eight-year-old for Twiston-Davies, won twice and placed seven times on comparable going, but the trainer's yard is winless in 14-day returns (0/8) and apprentice rider Toby McCain-Mitchell adds an unknown quantity — the race shape is entirely built around his ability to dictate.

runners_data.name: Most Wanted
runners_data.note: Won on Good ground over this exact 16f trip most recently (OR 90), wears headgear and is proven at Uttoxeter's distance; Brendan Powell rides for Bridgwater and this horse's recent winning run makes it one of the most interesting profile fits despite a hold-up tag — if it chooses to race closer, it becomes a genuine threat.

runners_data.name: Feet On The Ground
runners_data.note: Fergal O'Brien in good form (T14 3/20) and Tom Broughton (3) takes the ride, but the horse's true preference is to race at the rear — shown here in midfield because of redistribution pressure — and its Good-going record at this trip is only 5 from 14 with no wins, limiting confidence at the price.

runners_data.name: Royal Rhythm
runners_data.note: A 10-year-old with a string of fifth-place finishes (55-55 in last four), including all recent runs on Good ground at 20f+; the step back to 2m is worth noting for a hold-up horse that habitually needs every yard of a longer trip, and the redistribution to midfield disguises a runner that will likely be further back than its mapped position suggests.

runners_data.name: Fond Farewell
runners_data.note: Shares the Greenall & Guerriero yard with Alshadhian (T14 0/3), and the Toby Wynne booking is low-key; form figures include a pull-up and unseated in two of the last four starts, with no wins or place finishes on comparable going — though 4th and 5th in most recent outings show it is at least completing, this runner's true running style sits at the rear rather than the midfield slot it occupies on the map.

runners_data.name: Prairie Queen
runners_data.note: Unexpectedly consistent form profile — 233-13 — with a win and three places in last five on Good ground, all over this 16f trip; Sue Gardner's 6-year-old is the freshest improver in the field and Sean Houlihan has experience placing hold-up types, making this an each-way profile worth tracking despite the low OR of 77.

runners_data.name: Walk The Plank
runners_data.note: Won over 16f Good ground earlier in career and shapes as a horse with residual ability, though recent form (5, 4, then finishing fifth back on Good) shows inconsistency; Dylan Johnston takes the ride for Clare Hobson (T14 0/4) and like several others here is mapped to midfield rather than its natural rear position, meaning its chance depends on getting a cleaner run than its redistribution implies.

runners_data.name: Getaway Jewel
runners_data.note: Brian Hughes is a standout jockey booking for Micky Hammond's 12-year-old, who posted a second and a third in recent starts on Good ground; the age flag is real — veterans at this level often run their race on ability alone — but Getaway Jewel's form is fresher than its lowly OR 71 suggests, and Hughes is capable of conjuring a big run if the pace scenario suits a late arrival.

races.paceDynamic: Electric Eddy is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner handicap chase over 2m at Uttoxeter, and with no genuine rival to press him from the outside, he is free to control the tempo from the front and set whatever gallop he chooses on Good ground. The field behind him is dominated by hold-up types — Alshadhian, Person Of Interest, Most Wanted, Prairie Queen, Walk The Plank, Getaway Jewel, Feet On The Ground, Royal Rhythm, and Fond Farewell all want to race at the back or midfield — creating a race where the front is largely uncontested and the battle will be fought from the home turn inward. This field holds far more hold-up types than the pace map can honestly show at the rear; Feet On The Ground, Royal Rhythm, Fond Farewell, Prairie Queen, Walk The Plank, and Getaway Jewel have all been redistributed to midfield positions, but Electric Eddy is the only horse genuinely likely to secure the front, with Most Wanted and Alshadhian the most plausible chasers from slightly closer. The tactical verdict is clear: a lone, uncontested leader on Good ground over 2m at Uttoxeter — a sharp, flat track that rewards those who travel smoothly and quicken — strongly favours a front-runner who can control fractions and hold on, though closers with a clean run from off the pace retain each-way claims if Electric Eddy compounds.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Electric Eddy Dictates Alone
scenarios.trigger: If Electric Eddy bowls along uncontested in front and sets a controlled, sustainable gallop that denies the closers any real target to pick off.
scenarios.body: Electric Eddy, OR 94, settles into his natural front-running role with no challenger to his lead, controlling fractions across the 2m trip until his rivals are committed too late; the race is effectively won before the last fence as any closers are left with too much ground to make up on a flat, sharp track.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closers Swamp The Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Electric Eddy sets a pace that is just fractionally too strong for the distance and the field closes him down from the final fence.
scenarios.body: The hold-up horses — particularly Alshadhian and Person Of Interest, who have both shown strong recent form on Good ground — get a clear run from the back and arrive with finishing momentum as Electric Eddy ties up; on a compact 2m circuit, the final run-in at Uttoxeter is long enough for true closers to reel in a tiring leader.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Challenger Presses And Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If one of the nominally mid-pack runners — Most Wanted or Walk The Plank — elects to race prominently and presses Electric Eddy sufficiently to weaken him before the last.
scenarios.body: Most Wanted, who won over this exact 16f trip on Good ground most recently and carries headgear, has the profile to sit just off Electric Eddy and pick him off late if the front-runner weakens; Walk The Plank also won over this course and distance configuration and could travel into the race from a tracking position to challenge.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddling Pace Suits Underrated Type
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is genuinely uneven or Electric Eddy slows dramatically after a fence error, scrambling the race and gifting a chaos beneficiary.
scenarios.body: A collapse in tempo mid-race would compress the field and hand an opportunity to a fresh, lower-rated type with something to prove — Prairie Queen has posted consistent placed form across recent Good-ground runs and Getaway Jewel showed form figures of 2-3 in recent starts; neither would be expected to win under a normal tempo but both could capitalise on a scrappy, slowly-run affair that negates the higher-rated closers.

watchPoints.text: Electric Eddy is the sole front-runner in a 10-runner field — if he makes an error at a fence early or races too freely with Toby McCain-Mitchell (3) aboard, the entire pace scenario collapses and the race becomes a lottery.

Most Wanted (Brendan Powell, headgear, recent winner over this exact trip) may elect to race far closer than its hold-up tag suggests — watch the early positioning; if he tracks Electric Eddy from second, he becomes a serious contender and could flip Scenario C into higher likelihood.

Prairie Queen's placed form across all five recent starts on Good ground is unusually consistent for a 77-rated runner, and Sean Houlihan has a light but shrewd book of rides — monitor if it gets a clean passage from mid-division, as it could outrun its odds in a compressed finish.

The Greenall & Guerriero pair (Alshadhian and Fond Farewell) both run here with a yard that is 0/3 in the 14-day returns window — trainer form is cold, and punters should note this applies to both runners regardless of individual form figures.

Person Of Interest's record shows twelve starts on comparable going from fifteen total, but four of the last six runs are unfinished or out of the frame (P, U, 6, 9) — Harry Cobden's booking is notable but the finishing pattern suggests a horse with question marks about consistency when the race gets serious.
